A. Opening Page

Why This Chapter Matters

Today, news travels very fast. A message in a class group, a short video, a screenshot, or a headline can influence how people think and act.

Di wilayah kepulauan dan pesisir, informasi yang akurat sangat penting, terutama tentang cuaca, transportasi laut, kegiatan sekolah, lingkungan pesisir, dan pengumuman komunitas. Karena itu, kamu perlu membaca berita dengan hati-hati sebelum mempercayai atau membagikannya.

Big Question:
How can we know whether a news story is factual, biased, clickbait, or fake?
Bagaimana kita mengetahui apakah sebuah berita itu faktual, bias, clickbait, atau palsu?

English sentence: Accurate news helps people make safe and responsible decisions.
Artinya: Berita yang akurat membantu orang membuat keputusan yang aman dan bertanggung jawab.

Gambar siswa belajar ditampilkan setengah halaman sesuai instruksi.

Read Carefully

Baca isi berita, bukan hanya headline.

Verify Responsibly

Periksa sumber, tanggal, lokasi, dan bukti.

Share Wisely

Jangan membagikan informasi yang belum jelas.

C. My Initial Understanding

Look at the Headlines

Read the following headlines and decide which ones sound factual and which ones sound like clickbait.

Factual?

Students Launch Literacy Campaign at Coastal Senior High School

Artinya: Siswa meluncurkan kampanye literasi di SMA wilayah pesisir.

Clickbait?

You Won’t Believe What Happened at School Yesterday!

Artinya: Kamu tidak akan percaya apa yang terjadi di sekolah kemarin!

Factual?

Local Students Clean Beach to Support Environmental Awareness

Artinya: Siswa setempat membersihkan pantai untuk mendukung kesadaran lingkungan.

Clickbait?

Shocking! This One Habit Can Make All Students Fail Exams!

Artinya: Mengejutkan! Satu kebiasaan ini bisa membuat semua siswa gagal ujian!

Discussion

  1. Which headlines sound factual?
  2. Which headlines sound like clickbait?
  3. What words make a headline emotional?
  4. What information is missing from headline number 2 and 4?
  5. Have you ever shared news without reading the full text?

E. Learning Input 1

What Is News Item Text?

A news item text is a factual text that informs readers, viewers, or listeners about an important, recent, and real event.

English sentence: A news item text reports a real event in a clear, factual, and organized way.
Artinya: News item text melaporkan peristiwa nyata dengan cara yang jelas, faktual, dan terstruktur.

Social Function

The social function of news item text is to inform people about current events.

English sentence: The purpose of news is to inform the public, not to manipulate emotions.
Artinya: Tujuan berita adalah memberi informasi kepada publik, bukan memanipulasi emosi.

Text TypePurposeExample
News ItemTo report a real eventA school literacy campaign was launched.
AnnouncementTo inform about an upcoming activityThe English Club meeting will be held on Friday.
RecountTo retell past experienceLast week, we joined a beach clean-up.
ReportTo describe general factsMangroves protect coastal areas.
OpinionTo express personal viewI believe students should read more news.
F. Learning Input 2

Generic Structure of News Item Text

1. Headline
The title of the news. It should be short, clear, factual, and informative.
Students Plant Mangroves to Protect Coastal Area
Siswa Menanam Mangrove untuk Melindungi Wilayah Pesisir.
2. Lead / Newsworthy Event
The opening paragraph. It usually answers the most important parts of 5W+1H.
A group of students planted 200 mangrove seedlings near a coastal area on Saturday morning.
Sekelompok siswa menanam 200 bibit mangrove di dekat wilayah pesisir pada Sabtu pagi.
3. Background Events
Details, sequence, causes, participants, and context.
The activity was organized by the school environment club.
Kegiatan tersebut diselenggarakan oleh klub lingkungan sekolah.
4. Source / Quote
A source or quote gives credibility to the news.
“Protecting the coast starts with small actions,” the club advisor stated.
“Melindungi pesisir dimulai dari tindakan kecil,” ujar pembina klub.
5. Closing
Final details or future plans.
The club plans to monitor the seedlings every month.
Klub tersebut berencana memantau bibit mangrove setiap bulan.

Common Student Mistakes

MistakeBetter Version
Using emotional words without evidenceUse factual and neutral words.
Writing only one paragraphOrganize the text into headline, lead, background, quote, and closing.
Forgetting time and placeAdd adverbial phrases of time and place.
Mixing opinion with factSeparate factual information from personal opinion.
Not mentioning sourceInclude a verified source or quote.

Sample Learning Text

Students Hold Digital Literacy Workshop at School

Students from the school media club held a digital literacy workshop at the school hall on Tuesday morning. The workshop was designed to help students identify reliable news, avoid clickbait, and verify information before sharing it online.

The activity was attended by Grade XII students and facilitated by English teachers and student journalists. During the workshop, students analyzed several online headlines and discussed whether the headlines were factual, biased, or misleading.

“Our students often receive information from social media. They need practical skills to check facts before sharing news,” the club advisor stated.

The workshop ended with a group challenge in which students rewrote clickbait headlines into factual headlines.

QuestionAnswer
Who?Students from the school media club, Grade XII students, English teachers, and student journalists.
What?They held a digital literacy workshop.
When?On Tuesday morning.
Where?At the school hall.
Why?To help students identify reliable news and verify information.
How?By analyzing headlines, discussing bias, and rewriting clickbait headlines.
H. Learning Input 4

Fact, Opinion, Claim, Bias, and Clickbait

Fact

A fact is information that can be proven true or false.

The workshop was held on Tuesday morning.
Lokakarya tersebut diadakan pada Selasa pagi.

Opinion

An opinion is a personal view, belief, or feeling.

The workshop was the most exciting event of the year.
Lokakarya tersebut adalah acara paling menyenangkan tahun ini.

Claim

A claim is a statement that may be true, but needs evidence.

The program helped all students become better news readers.
Program tersebut membantu semua siswa menjadi pembaca berita yang lebih baik.

Bias

Bias is a one-sided presentation of information.

The report only interviewed students who liked the program.
Laporan tersebut hanya mewawancarai siswa yang menyukai program itu.

Misinformation

False or inaccurate information shared without intention to harm.

A student shared the wrong event date because he did not check the schedule.
Seorang siswa membagikan tanggal acara yang salah karena ia tidak memeriksa jadwal.

Disinformation

False information shared intentionally to mislead people.

Someone created a fake announcement to confuse students.
Seseorang membuat pengumuman palsu untuk membingungkan siswa.

Verification

The process of checking whether information is accurate.

Students verified the news by asking the teacher and checking the official announcement.
Siswa memverifikasi berita dengan bertanya kepada guru dan memeriksa pengumuman resmi.

Language Features

1. Saying Verbs

Saying verbs are verbs used to report what someone said. In news writing, saying verbs help writers include sources, quotes, and statements.

  1. The principal __________ that the ceremony would begin at 7.30 a.m.
  2. The student reporter __________ that the beach clean-up involved 80 volunteers.
  3. The post __________ that the school was closed, but it gave no evidence.
  4. The teacher __________ students to verify the information before sharing it.
  5. The committee __________ the results after checking all scores.

2. Passive Voice in Journalism

Passive voice is often used in news writing when the action or event is more important than the person who did it.

Future Passivewill be + V3The newsletter will be shared tomorrow.Buletin itu akan dibagikan besok.

K. Reading Section

Reading News Item Texts

Reading Text 1 — Students Launch Literacy Campaign to Promote Responsible News Reading

Students at a coastal senior high school launched a literacy campaign on Monday morning to encourage responsible news reading among teenagers. The campaign was held at the school hall and attended by Grade XII students, teachers, and members of the school media club.

The event began with a short presentation about how online news spreads through social media. Students were introduced to the differences between factual headlines, opinion-based posts, and clickbait. They also practiced checking the source, date, author, and evidence in several sample news articles.

The school media club reported that many students often read only headlines before sharing news in group chats. To respond to this habit, the club created posters with the message “Read First, Check Facts, Share Wisely.”

“Our students are active digital users. They need to become careful readers, not just fast sharers,” the English teacher stated during the session.

At the end of the campaign, students worked in groups to rewrite misleading headlines into factual headlines. The school plans to continue the program through monthly digital literacy activities.

Terjemahan dan Analisis

Siswa di sebuah SMA wilayah pesisir meluncurkan kampanye literasi pada Senin pagi untuk mendorong kebiasaan membaca berita secara bertanggung jawab. Kegiatan tersebut diadakan di aula sekolah dan diikuti oleh siswa kelas XII, guru, serta anggota klub media sekolah.

Kegiatan diawali dengan presentasi singkat tentang bagaimana berita online menyebar melalui media sosial. Siswa dikenalkan pada perbedaan antara judul faktual, unggahan berbasis opini, dan clickbait. Mereka juga berlatih memeriksa sumber, tanggal, penulis, dan bukti dalam beberapa contoh artikel berita.

QuestionAnswer
Who?Students, teachers, and school media club members.
What?They launched a literacy campaign.
When?On Monday morning.
Where?At the school hall.
Why?To encourage responsible news reading.
How?Through presentations, poster creation, and headline rewriting.

Questions

  1. What was launched by the students?
  2. Where was the campaign held?
  3. Why did the media club create posters?
  4. Why is reading only the headline risky?
  5. Find one saying verb and one passive voice sentence.

Reading Text 2 — Beach Clean-Up Program Raises Environmental Awareness Among Students

A beach clean-up program was conducted by senior high school students near a coastal area on Saturday morning. The activity was organized to raise awareness about plastic waste and its impact on marine life.

The program involved 90 students, several teachers, and local volunteers. Before the clean-up began, students received a safety briefing and were divided into small groups. Each group was assigned to collect plastic bottles, food wrappers, and other non-organic waste along the beach.

According to the student council, more than 25 bags of waste were collected during the activity. The collected waste was later sorted into recyclable and non-recyclable materials.

“Plastic waste can damage the coastal environment if people do not manage it properly,” the student council leader explained. He added that students should not only clean the beach but also reduce single-use plastic in daily life.

Gambar siswa field reporting: setengah halaman.

  3. Does the report sound objective? Explain your answer.

Reading Text 3 — Shocking! Students Panic After Dangerous Sea News Goes Viral

A viral message about “extremely dangerous sea conditions” was widely shared in several student group chats on Thursday night. The message claimed that all boat transportation would be cancelled the next morning, but it did not mention any official source, date, or clear location.

Some students became worried because they depend on sea transportation to reach school or return home. However, the school administration later confirmed that the message had not been verified. Students were asked to wait for official information from reliable sources.

The student media club reviewed the message and found several problems. First, the headline used emotional words such as “shocking” and “panic.” Second, the message did not include the name of the authority that issued the warning. Third, the screenshot was cropped and did not show the original link.

“The message may contain useful concern, but students must not treat it as confirmed news without verification,” the media club editor stated.

The school reminded students to check official announcements before making decisions related to transportation and safety.

Analysis Table
ProblemEvidence from TextWhy It Matters
Emotional headline“Shocking” and “panic”It may manipulate readers.
No official sourceNo authority mentionedReaders cannot verify it.
No clear date/locationMissing contextIt may refer to another place/time.
Cropped screenshotOriginal link missingThe information may be incomplete.

Critical Questions

  1. Why is the headline potentially clickbait?
  2. What information is missing from the viral message?
  3. Is the message definitely fake? Explain carefully.
  4. How can students verify sea transportation information responsibly?
L. Viewing Section

Viewing an Online News Page

Imagine you see an online news post with the headline: “Terrifying Weather Will Hit All Coastal Areas Tomorrow!” The source is unknown, the date is not shown, and no official data is provided.

Is This News Reliable?

QuestionYes/NoNotes
Is the source clear?________

English sentence: A scary image does not always prove that the news is accurate.
Artinya: Gambar yang menakutkan tidak selalu membuktikan bahwa berita itu akurat.

M. Listening Section

News Broadcast Script with TTS

Gunakan tombol TTS untuk menyimak script. Kamu juga dapat mengklik setiap kalimat untuk mendengarkan ulang bagian tertentu.

Buka/Tutup Script Listening
Good morning, everyone. You are listening to Student News Today. I am Rina, and here is our main report. A digital literacy campaign was held at a coastal senior high school on Wednesday morning. The event was organized by the school media club to help students identify reliable news and avoid spreading false information. The campaign began at 8 a.m. in the school hall. More than one hundred students attended the activity. During the session, students learned how to check news sources, publication dates, author names, and supporting evidence. The club advisor stated that students often receive news from social media before checking whether the information is true. She emphasized that responsible sharing is an important skill for young digital citizens. Several students were interviewed after the event. One student said that he would be more careful before forwarding messages in group chats. Another student added that factual headlines are more helpful than emotional headlines. The school media club will publish a digital newsletter next month. The newsletter will report verified school and community events. That is the report for today. Remember: read carefully, verify responsibly, and share wisely.
Terjemahan Script

Selamat pagi, semuanya. Kamu sedang mendengarkan Student News Today. Saya Rina, dan inilah laporan utama kami. Kampanye literasi digital diadakan di sebuah SMA wilayah pesisir pada Rabu pagi. Kegiatan tersebut diselenggarakan oleh klub media sekolah untuk membantu siswa mengenali berita yang dapat dipercaya dan menghindari penyebaran informasi palsu. Kampanye dimulai pukul 8 pagi di aula sekolah. Lebih dari seratus siswa mengikuti kegiatan tersebut. Selama sesi, siswa belajar cara memeriksa sumber berita, tanggal publikasi, nama penulis, dan bukti pendukung. Pembina klub menyatakan bahwa siswa sering menerima berita dari media sosial sebelum memeriksa apakah informasi tersebut benar. Ia menekankan bahwa berbagi informasi secara bertanggung jawab adalah keterampilan penting bagi warga digital muda. Beberapa siswa diwawancarai setelah acara. Seorang siswa mengatakan bahwa ia akan lebih berhati-hati sebelum meneruskan pesan di grup chat. Siswa lain menambahkan bahwa judul faktual lebih membantu daripada judul emosional. Klub media sekolah akan menerbitkan buletin digital bulan depan. Buletin tersebut akan melaporkan kegiatan sekolah dan komunitas yang telah diverifikasi.

Gap Filling

  1. A digital literacy campaign was held at a coastal senior high school on morning.
  2. The event was organized by the .
  3. Students learned how to check sources, dates, author names, and .
  4. Responsible sharing is an important skill for young .
  5. The media club will publish a digital next month.

True/False

  2. Fewer than fifty students attended the activity.

N. Speaking Section

Reporter Role-Play and Newsroom Discussion

Useful Expressions

Gambar broadcast-style final project: setengah halaman.

Model Conversation 1: Reporter and Student

Reporter: Good morning. Could you tell me what happened at school yesterday?
Selamat pagi. Bisakah kamu memberi tahu saya apa yang terjadi di sekolah kemarin?

Student: A digital literacy workshop was held at the school hall.
Lokakarya literasi digital diadakan di aula sekolah.

Reporter: Why was the workshop important?
Mengapa lokakarya tersebut penting?

Student: It helped us check facts before sharing news online.
Kegiatan itu membantu kami memeriksa fakta sebelum membagikan berita secara online.

Model Conversation 2: Editor Checks a Headline

Editor: This headline says, “Shocking Event Makes All Students Panic!” Is it factual?
Judul ini berbunyi, “Peristiwa Mengejutkan Membuat Semua Siswa Panik!” Apakah ini faktual?

Reporter: Not really. It sounds emotional and exaggerated.
Tidak sepenuhnya. Judul itu terdengar emosional dan berlebihan.

Reporter: Better headline: “Students Attend Safety Briefing Before School Trip.”
Judul yang lebih baik: “Siswa Mengikuti Pengarahan Keselamatan Sebelum Perjalanan Sekolah.”

Model Conversation 3: Checking Credibility

Student A: I saw a message saying that all boats are cancelled tomorrow.
Saya melihat pesan yang mengatakan bahwa semua kapal dibatalkan besok.

Student B: Where did the message come from?
Dari mana pesan itu berasal?

Student A: I am not sure. It was shared in a group chat.
Saya tidak yakin. Pesan itu dibagikan di grup chat.

Student B: We should check the official source before believing it.
Kita sebaiknya memeriksa sumber resmi sebelum mempercayainya.

Model News Anchor Introduction

Good morning, everyone. Welcome to Student News Today. I am your anchor, and this is our main report. A digital literacy campaign was held at our school on Monday morning. The event was organized to help students become more responsible digital citizens.

Selamat pagi, semuanya. Selamat datang di Student News Today. Saya pembawa berita Anda, dan inilah laporan utama kami. Kampanye literasi digital diadakan di sekolah kami pada Senin pagi. Kegiatan tersebut diselenggarakan untuk membantu siswa menjadi warga digital yang lebih bertanggung jawab.

O. Writing Section

Writing a News Item Text

Writing Steps

  1. Choose a real, verified event.
  2. Collect facts using 5W+1H.
  3. Write a factual headline.
  4. Write the lead.
  5. Add background events.
  6. Add a source or quote.
  7. Use saying verbs, passive voice, and adverbial phrases.
  8. Revise for objectivity and accuracy.

Headline Revision

Bad headline: Shocking! Students Did Something Amazing at School!
Mengejutkan! Siswa Melakukan Sesuatu yang Luar Biasa di Sekolah!

Better headline: Students Hold Digital Literacy Campaign at School
Siswa Mengadakan Kampanye Literasi Digital di Sekolah

Writing Template

Headline: __________________________

Lead: A/An __________ was held/organized/conducted at __________ on __________ to __________.

Background Events: The activity involved __________. During the activity, __________.

Source/Quote: “__________,” __________ stated/reported/explained/confirmed.

Closing: The school/community plans to __________.

Verification Note: This news was verified by checking official announcement / teacher confirmation / direct observation / interview / photo evidence.

Joint Construction Example

Students Create Newsletter to Promote Verified School News

A digital newsletter was created by the school media club on Friday afternoon to promote verified school news. The newsletter was designed to help students read factual information about school activities.

The project involved student reporters, editors, designers, and fact-checkers. Each team was responsible for collecting data, interviewing sources, checking facts, and designing the newsletter layout.

The media club advisor stated that the project trained students to become responsible digital journalists. She also explained that students should not publish information without verification.

The first edition of the newsletter will be shared with students next week through the school’s digital platform.

Terjemahan

Buletin digital dibuat oleh klub media sekolah pada Jumat sore untuk mempromosikan berita sekolah yang terverifikasi. Buletin tersebut dirancang untuk membantu siswa membaca informasi faktual tentang kegiatan sekolah. Proyek tersebut melibatkan reporter siswa, editor, desainer, dan pemeriksa fakta. Setiap tim bertanggung jawab mengumpulkan data, mewawancarai narasumber, memeriksa fakta, dan mendesain tata letak buletin. Pembina klub media menyatakan bahwa proyek tersebut melatih siswa menjadi jurnalis digital yang bertanggung jawab. Ia juga menjelaskan bahwa siswa tidak boleh menerbitkan informasi tanpa verifikasi. Edisi pertama buletin akan dibagikan kepada siswa minggu depan melalui platform digital sekolah.

P. Mini Lab

Before You Share: Verify It!

You will practice checking whether information is verified, uncertain, or misleading.

Steps

  1. Choose one simple school/community event.
  2. Write the headline or claim.
  3. Check the source.
  4. Check the date.
  5. Check the location.
  6. Look for evidence.
  7. Compare with at least two other sources.
  8. Interview a relevant person.
  9. Decide: verified, uncertain, or misleading.
  10. Write a short verification note.

Useful Sentences

The information was verified through an official announcement.
Informasi tersebut diverifikasi melalui pengumuman resmi.

The claim is uncertain because the source is unclear.
Klaim tersebut belum pasti karena sumbernya tidak jelas.

The post may be misleading because it uses an old photo.
Unggahan tersebut mungkin menyesatkan karena menggunakan foto lama.

Location
Evidence
Other Source 1
Other Source 2
Interviewed Person

Diagnostic, Formative, and Summative Assessment

Diagnostic Assessment

Grammar Practice

Active to Passive Answer Key
  1. The workshop was organized by the media club.
  2. The session was opened by the English teacher.
  3. Plastic waste was collected by students along the beach.
  4. The schedule was confirmed by the committee.
  5. Two students were interviewed by the reporter.

True/False with Reasons

  1. A news headline should always be emotional.
  2. Passive voice is often used in journalism.
  3. A claim always needs evidence.
  4. A screenshot is always reliable.
  5. News item text reports real events.
  6. Saying verbs can introduce quotes.
  7. Clickbait headlines are always the best headlines.
  8. Adverbial phrases can show time and place.
  9. Verification is important before sharing information.
  10. A balanced report may include more than one perspective.
Kunci Jawaban Benar/Salah
  1. False — headline should be factual and clear.
  2. True — passive voice is common in news.
  3. True — claims must be supported.
  4. False — screenshots can be edited or incomplete.
  5. True — news item text reports real events.
  6. True — stated, reported, explained, and confirmed introduce statements.
  7. False — clickbait can mislead readers.
  8. True — examples: on Monday, at the school hall.
  9. True — verification prevents misinformation.
  10. True — balanced reporting avoids one-sided information.

Essay Questions

  1. Explain the difference between fact and opinion. Give one example of each.
  2. Why is clickbait dangerous for students?
  3. How can students verify news about school or community events?
  4. Write a short news lead about a school activity.
  5. Explain why passive voice is useful in journalism.

S. Final Project

Digital Journalist Project

Option 1: Broadcast-Style Video News Report

Your group creates a 3–5 minute video news report about a verified school/community event.

Option 2: Mockup Newsletter

Your group creates a one-page or two-page newsletter about a verified school/community event.

Project Requirements

  1. a factual headline;
  2. 5W+1H information;
  3. at least one verified source;
  4. at least one quote;
  5. at least five saying verbs;
  6. at least five passive voice sentences;
  7. at least five adverbial phrases of time/place;
  8. a verification note;
  9. objective language;
  10. no fake news and no unverified claims.

Group Roles

RoleResponsibility
AnchorOpens and closes the broadcast.
Field ReporterReports from the event location.
InterviewerInterviews sources.
ScriptwriterWrites the news script.
Fact-CheckerChecks source, date, evidence, and quote.
EditorRevises language and structure.
DesignerDesigns newsletter or visual layout.
Camera/Audio PersonRecords video and checks sound quality.

Project Timeline

StageActivity
Day 1Choose event and assign roles
Day 2Collect data and conduct interviews
Day 3Write 5W+1H and draft script/article
Day 4Revise language features
Day 5Record video or design newsletter
Day 6Final checking and presentation

Rubrics

Rubric4321
Reading and ViewingIdentifies main ideas, details, structure, bias, and credibility accurately.Identifies main ideas and most details with minor mistakes.Understands some information but misses important details.Has difficulty understanding the text and identifying reliable information.
Speaking/BroadcastSpeaks clearly, uses correct news structure, accurate facts, good pronunciation, and confident delivery.Speaks clearly with minor grammar or pronunciation errors.Delivers limited information with several pauses or unclear parts.Presentation is unclear and lacks important news elements.
Writing News ItemComplete structure, factual content, strong 5W+1H, correct language features, and clear organization.Complete structure with minor language or detail errors.Some structure is missing; facts and language features need improvement.Text is incomplete, unclear, or not factual.
Final ProjectProject is factual, creative, well-organized, verified, and uses required language features.Project is clear and mostly verified with minor weaknesses.Project has limited verification or incomplete language features.Project lacks verification and does not follow news structure.
CollaborationAll members contribute actively and responsibly.Most members contribute well.Some members contribute, but teamwork is uneven.Collaboration is weak and tasks are not completed properly.
Critical Media LiteracyAccurately identifies fact, opinion, claim, bias, clickbait, and verification needs.Identifies most media literacy elements correctly.Identifies some elements but needs guidance.Has difficulty distinguishing factual and misleading information.
